prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Production artwork for the Mars combination game, in the established realistic painterly retro-industrial style: cream factory equipment, muted teal habitat fittings, cobalt scientific fittings, mustard mobility accents, ochre Martian terrain, modest wear. Local construction is simple cut and bolted straight steel, cloth and foil; imported pressure vessels and instruments retain their precision. No people, lettering, captions, labels, numbers, border graphics or UI. Generate COMPLETE SCENES, not isolated items. Every state has the exact SAME CAMERA, perspective, geography, light, object size and position. Change ONLY the named construction state. Leave generous quiet foreground for movable supplies. The lower half is simple natural ground or floor, not extra equipment. These paintings will be registered and cropped into background and changing fixed objects. Recurring items must retain their exact design. Reference images establish design and style, not an invitation to add all their objects.
Create a single WIDE LANDSCAPE scene-state sheet: 3 equal SQUARE full-scene panels in 1 row(s) and 3 columns. Each panel is SQUARE, not a narrow portrait strip. The complete sheet has aspect ratio 3:1. Arrange states in reading order. The full room or outdoor worksite is shown in each square scene; extra gameplay foreground is framed separately during export.
SCENE: Outside the same small ROUND cream starter habitat shown in the landing reference. It has the same right-side clamped patch. Do not make a long barrel habitat. The dome sits behind the work, around the upper middle. A bare panel plot at lower left and the compact atmospheric processing cabinet at lower right are separated by a clear working aisle. An existing feeder runs from the panel plot to an exterior wall distribution socket beside the processor. A prominent high antenna bracket is on the habitat roof/right side. The array is outdoors in sunlight. All useful equipment occupies the upper 52% of each frame, with empty red foreground below. No second habitat or lander in this closer working view.
STATE 1: The left solar installation plot is empty, with the existing feeder connector waiting on the ground. The processor is positioned but unplugged and inactive. The high radio bracket is empty.
STATE 2: The supplied dark photovoltaic panels are deployed on simple bolted steel supports on the left plot and connected to the waiting feeder. The processor remains unplugged. The radio bracket remains empty.
STATE 3: Exactly the same installed array. A short power patch cable now joins the processor to the adjacent exterior distribution outlet, and its small operating indicator is lit. The repaired dish is fitted to the high bracket; dish and support only, no portable radio box.
Keep the round habitat modest, with the solar plot and processor arranged on either side. Do not stack them down a tall narrow frame. Include a readable solar charging socket near the panels. Every habitat wall is already PATCHED; no open puncture remains.
